definition_title: Register subspaces: coordinate projections and linear maps on a register subspace
natural_language_statement:
Throughout, $F$ is a semiring (a finite field in every use), $\iota$ a type of coordinates with decidable equality, and the ambient space is $V = F^{\iota}$ (`ι → F`). A *register subspace* $V_S$ is the span of the standard basis vectors indexed by a finite set $S$ of coordinates (`S : Finset ι`), so it is determined by $S$. This bundle fixes the two pieces of vocabulary in which the conditionally linear machinery is written.

**Coordinate projections.** `MIPRE.CL.proj S` is the $F$-linear endomorphism of $F^{\iota}$ that keeps the coordinates in $S$ and zeroes the others, the projection onto $V_S$ along the complementary register subspace $V_{S^{c}}$ (the paper's $x \mapsto x^{V_S}$):
$$(\mathrm{proj}_S\,x)_i = \begin{cases} x_i & \text{if } i \in S,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

**Linear maps on a register subspace.** `MIPRE.CL.RegLinear F S` is a structure with two fields: an endomorphism `toLinearMap` $L$ of the ambient space, and the equation `proj_comp_proj'`, $\mathrm{proj}_S(L(\mathrm{proj}_S x)) = L\,x$ for all $x$. Such an $L$ reads only the coordinates in $S$ and writes only there; it stands for the paper's $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$, and the paper's shorthand $x^{L_1} = L_1(x^{V_1})$ becomes literally $L_1 x$. The bundle gives `RegLinear F S` a coercion to functions $F^{\iota} \to F^{\iota}$ (`instFunLikeForall`) and a zero element (`instZero`, the zero map). Four constructions: `RegLinear.id S`, the identity of $V_S$, which is $\mathrm{proj}_S$ on the ambient space; `RegLinear.ofLinearMap S L`, the compression $\mathrm{proj}_S \circ L \circ \mathrm{proj}_S$ of an arbitrary endomorphism $L$; `RegLinear.castLE h L`, the same underlying map regarded as a map on $V_T$ when $h : S \subseteq T$; and `RegLinear.directSum L M`, the sum $L + M$ of a map on $V_S$ and a map on $V_T$ as a map on $V_{S \cup T}$ (their direct sum when $S$ and $T$ are disjoint).

The embedded lemmas are the `simp` equations of these objects: the evaluation rule of $\mathrm{proj}_S$; $\mathrm{proj}_S \circ \mathrm{proj}_T = \mathrm{proj}_{S \cap T}$ with its special cases (idempotence, $\mathrm{proj}_{\emptyset} = 0$, $\mathrm{proj}$ of the whole finite index set is the identity, and the two forms for $S \subseteq T$); the coercion lemmas, the linear-map-class instance and extensionality for `RegLinear`; the invariance facts $\mathrm{proj}_S(Lx) = Lx$ and $L(\mathrm{proj}_S x) = Lx$, also with any $T \supseteq S$ in place of $S$; and the evaluation rules of `0`, `id`, `ofLinearMap`, `castLE` and `directSum`.

**Formalization Note**. There is a single ambient space `ι → F` throughout; a register subspace is never a subtype but the finite set `S` of its coordinates, and a map "on $V_S$" is an endomorphism of the ambient space satisfying the invariance equation, which is how the paper's $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and $L_{k,u} : V_{k,u} \to V_{k,u}$ are represented without dependent-type transport. Only `[Semiring F]` and `[DecidableEq ι]` are assumed; `proj_univ` additionally needs `[Fintype ι]`. Nothing here depends on the field size.
source: https://github.com/vidick/MIPRE-formalization/blob/70cbf1c52e3d5e1dff1162fdf952c9a9f4bd99ed/MIPRE/Foundations/CL/Register.lean; companion paper (vidick/MIPRE-proof), linear.tex and preliminaries.tex ("Register subspace")

definition_title: Conditionally linear functions: presentations, evaluation, support, marginals and stage data
natural_language_statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring and $\iota$ a type of coordinates with decidable equality; the ambient space is $F^{\iota}$ with its register subspaces $V_S$ and projections $\mathrm{proj}_S$ (bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_CL_Register`). The paper defines the $\ell$-level conditionally linear (CL) functions on $V$ inductively: the $0$-level one is the zero function, and an $\ell$-level one has the form $L(x) = L_1(x^{V_1}) + L_{>1,\,L_1(x^{V_1})}(x^{V_{>1}})$ for complementary register subspaces $V_1 \oplus V_{>1} = V$, a linear map $L_1$ on $V_1$ and $(\ell-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,v}$ on $V_{>1}$. This bundle formalizes the *decomposition data*, which the function does not determine and which everything downstream uses (blueprint `def:cl-function`).

**Presentations.** `MIPRE.CL.CLFun F ι ℓ` is an inductive type with constructors `zero : CLFun F ι 0` and `cons S L₁ next : CLFun F ι (ℓ + 1)`, for a finite set of coordinates $S$, a map $L_1$ on $V_S$ (`RegLinear F S`) and a continuation `next : (ι → F) → CLFun F ι ℓ` indexed by the value of $L_1$. For $\iota$ finite, `CLFun.eval` is the function presented: $\mathrm{eval}(\mathtt{zero}) = 0$ and
$$\mathrm{eval}(\mathtt{cons}\,S\,L_1\,\mathit{next})(x) = L_1 x + \mathrm{eval}\bigl(\mathit{next}(L_1 x)\bigr)\bigl(\mathrm{proj}_{S^{c}}\,x\bigr).$$
`CLFun.SupportedOn P T` says that $P$ is a presentation on $V_T$: `zero` is on every $V_T$, and `cons S L₁ next` is on $V_T$ when $S \subseteq T$ and every `next v` is on $V_{T \setminus S}$. `CLFun.ExactlyOn P T` is the strengthening in which `zero` is on $V_T$ only for $T = \emptyset$, so that the register subspaces used along every run partition $T$ (item (2) of the structure lemma).

**Levels.** `CLFun.lift T P` adds one trivial level at the bottom, the register subspace $V_T$ with the zero map (`cons S L₁ next` lifts to `cons S L₁ (fun v => (next v).lift (T \ S))`); `CLFun.liftN T n P` adds $n$ of them. `CLFun.truncate k P` keeps the first $k$ levels, the $k$-th marginal $L_{\le k}$: `truncate 0 P = zero`, `truncate (k+1) (cons S L₁ next) = cons S L₁ (fun v => truncate k (next v))`, and `truncate (k+1) zero` pads with trivial levels on $\emptyset$.

**Stage data.** `CLFun.factorAt P k x` (a `Finset ι`) and `CLFun.mapAt P k x` (an endomorphism of the ambient space) are the register subspace and the linear map applied at stage $k+1$ on the input $x$: at `cons S L₁ next` they are $S$ and $L_1$ for $k = 0$ and recurse into `next (L₁ x)` on $\mathrm{proj}_{S^c} x$ for $k + 1$; beyond the level of $P$ they are $\emptyset$ and $0$. `CLFun.factorOfPrefix P k u` and `CLFun.mapOfPrefix P k u` compute the same data from the prefix $u = L_{\le k}(x)$ instead of $x$, recursing into `next (proj S u)` on $\mathrm{proj}_{S^c} u$; they are what the `factor` and `linear` queries of a sampler answer.

The embedded lemmas are the defining equations of all of the above, constructor by constructor, as `simp` lemmas; that every level-$0$ presentation is `zero`; that `lift` and `liftN` preserve `eval` and that `eval` vanishes at $0$ and on truncations of `zero`; and `truncate_self`: $P.\mathrm{truncate}\,\ell = P$.

**Formalization Note**. Two departures from the paper, both harmless: continuations are indexed by all vectors rather than by the values of $L_1$ (the others are never evaluated), and there is one ambient space throughout, $V_{>1}$ being $V_{T \setminus S}$ and not stored, since the level-$0$ presentation is the zero function on every $V_{T'}$. `eval`, `factorAt`, `mapAt` and the prefix versions assume `[Fintype ι]` (for the complement $S^{c}$); the rest only `[Semiring F]` and `[DecidableEq ι]`. `IsCLFun` and the theorems of the structure lemma `lem:cl-structure` are in the source module but not among the declarations of this bundle.

definition_title: Closure of conditionally linear presentations: concatenation, direct sums and the CL distribution
natural_language_statement:
Let $F$ be a semiring, $\iota$ a type of coordinates with decidable equality, and `CLFun F ι ℓ` the $\ell$-level presentations of conditionally linear functions on $F^{\iota}$ (bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_CL_Basic`). This bundle has the two constructions of the paper's closure lemmas and the question distribution of a pair of CL functions. The constructions carry no hypotheses; the disjointness hypotheses of the paper enter only in the evaluation lemmas, which are proved in the source module.

**Concatenation** (`lem:cl-concat`). `CLFun.concat L R`, for $L$ of level $k$ and a family $R$ of presentations of level $\ell$ indexed by vectors, is a presentation of level $\ell + k$: run $L$, then the $R_u$ selected by its output $u$. The clauses are `concat zero R = R 0` and `concat (cons S L₁ next) R = cons S L₁ (fun v => (next v).concat (fun w => R (v + w)))`, the output accumulated so far being passed along. For $L$ on $V_U$ and the $R_u$ on $V_W$ with $U$, $W$ disjoint, it presents the paper's $T(x) = L(x^{U}) + R_{L(x^{U})}(x^{W})$.

**Direct sums** (`lem:cl-func-prod`, two summands). `CLFun.directSum P Q`, for $P$, $Q$ of the same level, joins the two presentations stage by stage: `directSum zero zero = zero` and `directSum (cons S L₁ next) (cons S' L₁' next') = cons (S ∪ S') (L₁.directSum L₁') (fun v => (next (proj S v)).directSum (next' (proj S' v)))`, each continuation being selected by its own component of the joint output. Summands of different levels are first padded to a common level with `liftN`.

**The CL distribution** (`def:cl-dist`). For $F$ and $\iota$ finite, `MIPRE.CL.clDist L R`, for any two functions $L, R : F^{\iota} \to F^{\iota}$, is the law of $(Lx, Rx)$ for $x$ uniform in $F^{\iota}$, as a real-valued probability mass function on pairs:
$$\mathrm{clDist}(L,R)(a,b) = \frac{\#\{x \in F^{\iota} : Lx = a \wedge Rx = b\}}{|F^{\iota}|}.$$

The embedded lemmas are the two defining equations of `concat` and of `directSum` as `simp` lemmas, and `clDist_nonneg` and `sum_clDist`: the distribution is nonnegative and sums to $1$ over all pairs (for $F$ nonempty).

**Formalization Note**. `concat` and `directSum` are defined on presentations with no side conditions, so a disjointness hypothesis never has to be carried through a construction; `SupportedOn.eval_concat`, `SupportedOn.eval_directSum`, the support lemmas and the statements about functions (`IsCLFun.concat`, `IsCLFun.directSum`) are in the source module and not among the declarations of this bundle. `clDist` is `noncomputable` (a real-valued quotient of cardinalities) and is in the format of the question distribution of a `MIPRE.Game`. The paper's third closure property, downsizing to $\mathbb{F}_2$ (`lem:cl-downsize`), needs self-dual bases and is not here.
source: https://github.com/vidick/MIPRE-formalization/blob/70cbf1c52e3d5e1dff1162fdf952c9a9f4bd99ed/MIPRE/Foundations/CL/Closure.lean; blueprint def:cl-function, lem:cl-closure; companion paper (vidick/MIPRE-proof), linear.tex, lem:cl-concat, lem:cl-func-prod and def:cl-dist

definition_title: Halting within a cost bound in the ambient cost model (addition to the published cost-model bundle)
natural_language_statement:
This bundle adds one declaration to the already published bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_Cost_Basic`, the ambient cost model of the formalization: programs `Prog` of a small first-order language on binary-tree data `Data`, the timed big-step semantics `Eval env p r t` ("in the environment $\mathit{env}$, the program $p$ halts with the result $r$ at cost $t$"), and `Halts p x`, which says that $p$ run on the input $x$ (the environment $[x]$) halts at some cost.

**Bounded halting.** `MIPRE.Cost.HaltsWithin p x t`, for a program $p$, an input $x$ and a budget $t \in \mathbb{N}$, says that $p$ halts on $x$ within cost $t$:
$$\mathrm{HaltsWithin}(p, x, t) \iff \exists\, r\ \exists\, t' \le t,\ \ \mathrm{Eval}([x],\, p,\, r,\, t').$$
This is the primitive in which the time bounds of the project are spelled out: the total time bound `TimeBound` of the same module (a bound as a function of the input size) and the sampler bound `Sampler.TimeBoundAt` of the bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_CL_Sampler` are both of the form "for every input in a class, `HaltsWithin` with a stated budget".

There are no embedded lemmas in this addition.

**Formalization Note**. The declaration is `MIPRE.Cost.HaltsWithin : Prog → Data → ℕ → Prop` of `MIPRE/Foundations/Cost/Basic.lean`; it was not among the declarations kept in the published cost-model bundle and is added here because the sampler bundle of this upload uses it. The cost $t'$ is the one charged by `Eval` (one unit per rule, plus the size of every value read or written as a literal); the budget $t$ is an upper bound, not an exact cost.

definition_title: Size bounds for the encodings of bits, bit strings, binary numbers, pairs and programs (addition to the published encoding bundle)
natural_language_statement:
This bundle adds eight lemmas, and no new definitions, to the already published bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_Cost_Encoding`, the interface between ordinary types and the ambient cost model: a `SizedEncoding α` renders $a : \alpha$ as a tree $\mathrm{encode}(a)$ of type `Data`, and $\mathrm{esize}(a)$ is the number of nodes of that tree. Bits are `Data.ofBool` ($\mathrm{false} \mapsto \mathtt{nil}$, $\mathrm{true} \mapsto \mathtt{cons}(\mathtt{nil},\mathtt{nil})$), lists are `Data.ofList f` ($\mathtt{cons}$-chains ending in $\mathtt{nil}$), bit strings `BitStr` are lists of bits, a natural number is its string of binary digits `Nat.bits` (least significant bit first), a pair is a single $\mathtt{cons}$, and a program $p$ is its tree serialization `Prog.toData p`.

The lemmas added, for a type with a `SizedEncoding` and $a$ in it, a bit $b$, a list $l$, a bit string $x$, a natural number $n$ and a program $p$: `esize_pos`, $0 < \mathrm{esize}(a)$; `Data.size_ofBool`, $\mathrm{size}(\mathrm{ofBool}\ b) \le 3$; `Data.size_ofList_le`, if $\mathrm{size}(f(a)) \le B$ for all $a$ then $\mathrm{size}(\mathrm{ofList}\ f\ l) \le (B+1)\,|l| + 1$; `esize_bitStr_le`, $\mathrm{esize}(x) \le 4|x| + 1$; `esize_nat_le`, with $|n|$ the binary length `Nat.size n`,
$$\mathrm{esize}(n) \le 4\,|n| + 1;$$
`encode_prod`, $\mathrm{encode}(a, b) = \mathtt{cons}(\mathrm{encode}\ a, \mathrm{encode}\ b)$; `Prog.esize_eq_size_toData`, $\mathrm{esize}(p) = \mathrm{size}(\mathrm{toData}\ p)$; and `Prog.two_le_esize`, $2 \le \mathrm{esize}(p)$, because `toData` is a $\mathtt{cons}$ node whatever the constructor, so no program encodes to $\mathtt{nil}$.

These are the upper bounds that make the encodings honest bit lengths up to a constant factor, and the last one is load-bearing: as its docstring records, it is what forces $2 \le \lambda$ in the boundedness predicate of normal form verifiers (`Verifier.IsBounded`), and so what puts the index of the halting reduction inside the range where its time clauses say anything.

**Formalization Note**. All eight are theorems of `MIPRE/Foundations/Cost/Encoding.lean` about definitions that are already published; `encode_prod` and `esize_eq_size_toData` hold by `rfl`. Nothing in the published bundle is changed; this delta only adds the declarations that the bundles of this upload use (the sampler bundle, through `encode` and `esize`). All bounds are non-strict except `esize_pos` and `two_le_esize`, which are stated exactly as $0 < \mathrm{esize}(a)$ and $2 \le \mathrm{esize}(p)$.

definition_title: Samplers: programs presenting two conditionally linear functions over $\mathbb{F}_2$ through the query interface
natural_language_statement:
A sampler (blueprint `def:sampler`) is the question-producing half of a normal form verifier: a program of the ambient cost model (`Prog`, bundles `MIPRE_Foundations_Cost_*`) which, on an index $n$, presents two $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions $L^{\mathsf A}, L^{\mathsf B}$ on $\mathbb{F}_2^{s(n)}$, one per player, through a fixed query interface; the question distribution of the game at index $n$ is the law of $(L^{\mathsf A}x, L^{\mathsf B}x)$ for $x$ uniform.

**Players, the field, bit strings.** `MIPRE.Player` is the inductive type `alice | bob`, with `Player.toBool` (Alice is `false`, Bob `true`), `Player.ofBool`, and a `SizedEncoding` through the bit. `MIPRE.CL.𝔽₂` is `ZMod 2`. Vectors of $\mathbb{F}_2^{s}$ travel as bit strings of length $s$: `toBits v` is the list of coordinates, `ofBits s l` reads a vector off a list (missing bits read as $0$, bits beyond $s$ are ignored), and `indicatorBits S` is the indicator string of a set of coordinates, the representation of a register subspace.

**Queries.** `MIPRE.CL.Sampler.Query` has the constructors `dimension`, `marginal w j z`, `linear w j u y` and `factor w j u`, for a player $w$, a level $j$ and bit strings $z, u, y$. `Query.toTuple` encodes a query as $(\mathit{kind}, w, j, u, y)$ with kinds $0,1,2,3$ and missing arguments empty, `Query.ofTuple` reads it back (`none` on an unknown kind), and `Query.instSizedEncoding` encodes a query as its tuple.

**Samplers.** `MIPRE.CL.Sampler ℓ` is a structure with fields `prog : Prog`; `closed : prog.WellScoped 1`; `dim : ℕ → ℕ`, the dimension $s(n)$; `cl : (n : ℕ) → Player → CLFun 𝔽₂ (Fin (dim n)) ℓ`, the two presented CL functions; `cl_exactlyOn`, each is `ExactlyOn Finset.univ`; and five run clauses, each saying that `prog` on the input $\mathrm{encode}(n, q)$ runs (`Prog.Runs`) to the encoded answer at some cost: `runs_dimension` answers $s(n)$; `runs_marginal`, for $1 \le j \le \ell$ and $|z| = s(n)$, answers $\mathrm{toBits}(L^{w}_{\le j}(\mathrm{ofBits}\,z))$ (via `truncate j`); `runs_linear`, for $1 \le j \le \ell$, $u$ in the image of $L^{w}_{< j}$ (some $x$ with $u = \mathrm{toBits}(L^{w}_{\le j-1}(x))$) and $|y| = s(n)$, answers $\mathrm{toBits}(L^{w}_{j,u}\,y)$ (via `mapOfPrefix (j-1)`); `runs_factor`, under the same conditions on $j$ and $u$, answers $\mathrm{indicatorBits}(V^{w}_{j,u})$ (via `factorOfPrefix (j-1)`); and `halts`: for every $n$ and every `d : Data`, `prog` halts on $\mathtt{cons}(\mathrm{encode}\,n, d)$. `Sampler.TimeBoundAt S n T k` is the time bound at index $n$ with coefficient $T$ and degree $k$,
$$\forall d : \mathrm{Data},\quad \mathrm{HaltsWithin}\bigl(S.\mathrm{prog},\ \mathtt{cons}(\mathrm{encode}\,n, d),\ T\,(\mathrm{size}(d)+1)^{k}\bigr);$$
`Sampler.size S` is the description length $|\mathcal S| = \mathrm{esize}(S.\mathrm{prog})$, and `Sampler.dist S n` is `clDist` of the two evaluated CL functions.

The embedded lemmas are the round trips `ofBool_toBool`, `ofTuple_toTuple`, `ofBits_toBits` and `toBits_ofBits` (for $|l| = s$), the length lemmas for `toBits` and `indicatorBits`, `TimeBoundAt.mono` (monotone in $T$ and $k$), and `dist_nonneg`, `sum_dist`.

**Formalization Note**. The field size is fixed at $2$, as for the blueprint's normal form verifiers, so the paper's representation over $\mathbb{F}_{2^k}$ through a self-dual basis is not needed. The correctness clauses are imposed exactly where the paper imposes them, and the program must halt on every input $(n, d)$, well formed or not; `TimeBoundAt` reads the supremum of running times at index $n$ as a polynomial bound in the size of the whole input, because the model has no cursor into its input and no bound uniform over all inputs is satisfiable by a program that walks a list of unbounded length. The private lemma `ite_decide_eq_one` is kept because `ofBits_toBits` uses it.
source: https://github.com/vidick/MIPRE-formalization/blob/70cbf1c52e3d5e1dff1162fdf952c9a9f4bd99ed/MIPRE/Foundations/CL/Sampler.lean; blueprint def:sampler; companion paper (vidick/MIPRE-proof), linear.tex, Definition def:sampler and def:sampler-sample

definition_title: Integers and Gaussian integers as pairs of naturals, with primitive recursive arithmetic
natural_language_statement:
Mathlib's `Primrec` has no arithmetic on $\mathbb{Z}$ (and no `Primcodable ℤ`), so the enumeration behind `lem:value-lower-approx` carries its integers as pairs of natural numbers. This bundle fixes that representation and its arithmetic; every function in it is primitive recursive, with the proof next to the definition.

**Integers.** `MIPRE.ValueApprox.PInt` is `ℕ × ℕ`, the pair $(a, b)$ denoting $a - b$, and `PInt.toInt (a, b) = a - b$ in $\mathbb{Z}$. The operations are `PInt.zero = (0, 0)`, `PInt.ofNat n = (n, 0)`, `PInt.ofInt m = (m.toNat, (-m).toNat)`, `PInt.add (a,b) (c,d) = (a+c, b+d)`, `PInt.neg (a,b) = (b,a)`, `PInt.mul (a,b) (c,d) = (ac+bd, ad+bc)`, and `PInt.sum`, the fold of `add` over a list. Equality and order are the semantic ones, `PInt.Eq' x y` $\iff x_1 + y_2 = y_1 + x_2$ and `PInt.Lt' x y` $\iff x_1 + y_2 < y_1 + x_2$, both with `Decidable` instances.

**Gaussian integers.** `MIPRE.ValueApprox.GInt` is `PInt × PInt`, the pair $(m, n)$ denoting $m + n i$, and `GInt.toC z` is the complex number $\mathrm{toInt}(z_1) + \mathrm{toInt}(z_2)\, i$. The operations are `GInt.zero`, `GInt.ofNat n`, `GInt.ofInt m n` (the two integer parts), componentwise `GInt.add`, the product `GInt.mul` computed as
$$(m + n i)(m' + n' i) = (mm' - nn') + (mn' + nm')\, i,$$
the conjugate `GInt.conj (m, n) = (m, -n)`, `GInt.sum` over a list, and semantic equality `GInt.Eq'` (both components `PInt.Eq'`), decidable.

The embedded lemmas say that `toInt` and `toC` commute with every operation (`toInt_zero`, `toInt_ofNat`, `toInt_ofInt`, `toInt_add`, `toInt_neg`, `toInt_mul`, `toInt_sum`; `toC_zero`, `toC_ofNat`, `toC_ofInt`, `toC_add`, `toC_mul`, `toC_conj`, `toC_sum`, with `re_toC`, `im_toC`), that `Eq'` and `Lt'` are equality and strict order of the denoted values (`eq'_iff`, `lt'_iff`), and that `ofNat`, `add`, `neg`, `mul`, `conj` and `sum` are `Primrec` while `Eq'` and `Lt'` are `PrimrecRel`.

**Formalization Note**. `PInt` and `GInt` are `abbrev`s for product types, so Mathlib's `Primcodable` instance for `ℕ × ℕ` applies unchanged and the `Primrec` proofs are compositions of `Primrec.pair`, `Primrec.nat_add`, `Primrec.nat_mul`, `Primrec.list_foldr`, `Primrec.eq` and `Primrec.nat_lt`. The representation is not canonical ($(a, b)$ and $(a+1, b+1)$ denote the same integer), which is why equality of denoted values is the relation `Eq'` and not equality of pairs. There is no `ofInt` for `PInt` taking a `GInt`; `GInt.ofInt` takes two integers.

definition_title: Nonlocal games, strategies and values: tensor-product, synchronous and commuting strategies
natural_language_statement:
The definitions of blueprint Section 2.1: two-player one-round games, the three classes of strategies, built on a common skeleton, and their values.

**Games.** `MIPRE.Game X Y A B`, for finite question alphabets $X, Y$ and answer alphabets $A, B$, has a question distribution `μ : X → Y → ℝ` (fields `μ_nonneg`, `μ_sum_one`) and a decision predicate `D : X → Y → A → B → Bool` (`def:game`). `MIPRE.SynchronousGame X A` (`def:sync-game`) has the same fields with $Y = X$, $B = A$, plus `synchronous`: $D(x,x,a,b) = \mathrm{false}$ for $a \ne b$; `SynchronousGame.toGame` forgets it.

**The skeleton.** `MIPRE.ProjectiveMeasurement X A 𝒜`, over a star ring $\mathcal A$, is a family `M : X → A → 𝒜` with `selfAdjoint` ($(M^a_x)^{*} = M^a_x$), `projective` ($M^a_x M^a_x = M^a_x$) and `normalized` ($\sum_a M^a_x = 1$); `ProjectiveMeasurement.map φ P` transports it along a star-algebra equivalence. `MIPRE.TracialState 𝒜`, over a complex star algebra, extends a linear functional $\tau : \mathcal A \to \mathbb{C}$ (coercion `instFunLikeComplex`) by positivity $0 \le \tau(m^{*}m)$ (in the order of $\mathbb{C}$), $\tau(1) = 1$ and $\tau(mn) = \tau(nm)$; `TracialState.comp τ φ` pulls it back along a star-algebra equivalence, and `MIPRE.normalizedTrace n` is $\tau(m) = \mathrm{Tr}(m)/|n|$ on `Matrix n n ℂ`. `MIPRE.tracialValue G τ P`, for a synchronous game $G$, is
$$\sum_{x,y}\sum_{a,b} \mu(x,y)\,[D(x,y,a,b)]\ \mathrm{Re}\,\tau\bigl(M^a_x M^b_y\bigr).$$
`MIPRE.POVM X d` (QuantumLib's definition): `mats : X → selfAdjoint (Matrix d d ℂ)`, each `nonneg` in the Loewner order, with `normalized` $\sum_x \mathrm{mats}_x = 1$.

**Strategies and values.** `MIPRE.TensorProductStrategy G` (`def:tensor-strategy`): dimensions `dA`, `dB`, a state `ψ : Fin dA × Fin dB → ℂ` with `ψ_unit` ($\psi^{*}\cdot\psi = 1$) and projective measurements `PA`, `PB` on the two matrix algebras; `TensorProductStrategy.value` is the Born sum $\sum \mu(x,y)[D(x,y,a,b)]\,\mathrm{Re}\langle\psi,(A^a_x \otimes B^b_y)\psi\rangle$ (Kronecker product), and `MIPRE.quantumValue G` $= \sup_S S.\mathrm{value}$ (`def:q-value`). `MIPRE.SyncStrategy G` (`def:sync-strategy`): a dimension `d` with `d_pos` and a projective measurement `P` on `Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ`; `SyncStrategy.value` is `tracialValue` against the normalized trace, `MIPRE.syncValue G` its supremum (`def:sync-value`), `SyncStrategy.IsPCC` (`def:pcc`) requires $M^a_x M^b_y = M^b_y M^a_x$ whenever $\mu(x,y) > 0$, and `SyncStrategy.povm S x` packages the measurements as POVMs. `MIPRE.CommutingStrategy G` (`def:commuting-strategy`): a type `alg : Type` with a `CStarAlgebra` instance, a tracial state `τ` and a projective measurement `P` in it; `CommutingStrategy.value` is `tracialValue G τ P` (`def:commuting-value`). `SyncStrategy.toCommutingStrategy` takes `alg = CStarMatrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ` with the normalized trace; `SyncStrategy.toTensorProductStrategy` plays $A^a_x = M^a_x$, $B^b_y = (M^b_y)^{\mathsf T}$ on `MIPRE.maxEntangled d` $= d^{-1/2}\sum_i |i\rangle|i\rangle$.

The embedded lemmas are the coercion lemmas of `TracialState` and the `simp` rules of `map`, `comp`, `normalizedTrace`; $0 \le S.\mathrm{value} \le 1$ for tensor-product strategies (through `posSemidef_kronecker` and $\sum_{a,b}\langle\psi,(A^a_x\otimes B^b_y)\psi\rangle = 1$), hence `bddAbove_range_value` and `quantumValue_nonneg`; `SyncStrategy.value_eq`, the explicit form $\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Tr}(M^a_xM^b_y)/d$; and `value_toCommutingStrategy` (by `rfl`) and `value_toTensorProductStrategy`, via $\langle\psi|M\otimes N|\psi\rangle = \mathrm{Tr}(MN^{\mathsf T})/d$ on the maximally entangled state.

**Formalization Note**. Distributions are bare real functions with nonnegativity and normalization fields, not `PMF`; every value takes the real part `.re`, so no definition carries a proof obligation; strategies are projective, following JNVWY (Naimark dilation loses no generality; general POVMs are vocabulary only); the algebra of a `CommutingStrategy` lives in universe `0` (no loss, by GNS). `commValue`, `entRequirement` and the comparison lemmas named in the module docstring are not among the declarations of this bundle.

definition_title: The perturbation split of Born expectations, groundwork for approximating the quantum value from below
natural_language_statement:
This bundle is the groundwork module of `lem:value-lower-approx` (the $\mathrm{MIP}^{*} \subseteq \mathrm{RE}$ direction). It contributes no definition and three exact algebraic identities about Born expectations $\langle\psi, M\psi\rangle = \psi^{*}\cdot(M\psi)$ (`star ψ ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ ψ)`) on $\mathbb{C}^{d}$, with no norms and no estimates, which let the two players' operators and the state of a candidate strategy be perturbed one at a time (blueprint `lem:perturbation-split`).

`MIPRE.ValueApprox.kronecker_sub_kronecker`: for square matrices $A, A'$ indexed by $d_A$ and $B, B'$ indexed by $d_B$ (arbitrary index types), $A \otimes B - A' \otimes B' = (A - A') \otimes B + A' \otimes (B - B')$.

`MIPRE.ValueApprox.dotProduct_mulVec_perturb`: for $M, N$ square matrices over a finite index type $d$ and vectors $\psi, \varphi : d \to \mathbb{C}$,
$$\langle\psi, M\psi\rangle - \langle\varphi, N\varphi\rangle = \langle\psi, (M-N)\psi\rangle + \langle\psi-\varphi, N\psi\rangle + \langle\varphi, N(\psi-\varphi)\rangle,$$
an operator term in which only $M - N$ appears plus two state terms in which only $\psi - \varphi$ appears.

`MIPRE.ValueApprox.dotProduct_kronecker_perturb`, the split a candidate strategy needs: for $d_A, d_B$ finite, $\langle\psi,(A\otimes B)\psi\rangle - \langle\varphi,(A'\otimes B')\varphi\rangle$ equals the sum of the four terms $\langle\psi,((A-A')\otimes B)\psi\rangle$, $\langle\psi,(A'\otimes(B-B'))\psi\rangle$, $\langle\psi-\varphi,(A'\otimes B')\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\varphi,(A'\otimes B')(\psi-\varphi)\rangle$, each moving exactly one of $A$, $B$ and $\psi$.

**Formalization Note**. `⬝ᵥ` is Mathlib's dot product and `*ᵥ` matrix-vector multiplication, so $\langle\psi, M\psi\rangle$ is `star ψ ⬝ᵥ (M *ᵥ ψ)` and no inner-product-space structure is involved; `⊗ₖ` is the Kronecker product on matrices indexed by the product type. The identities are equalities in $\mathbb{C}$ and in matrices respectively, with no hypotheses on the matrices or vectors. The decidability statements of the module docstring (operator-norm constraints as positive-semidefiniteness tests) are not among the declarations of this bundle.

definition_title: The Cayley transform between skew-Hermitian matrices and unitaries
natural_language_statement:
Let $n$ be a finite index type with decidable equality and consider complex $n \times n$ matrices. `MIPRE.ValueApprox.IsSkewHermitian S` is the predicate $S^{\mathsf H} = -S$ (conjugate transpose), and `MIPRE.ValueApprox.cayley S` is the Cayley transform
$$\mathrm{cayley}(S) = (1 - S)\,(1 + S)^{-1},$$
with Mathlib's matrix inverse (which is $0$ on a singular matrix, so the definition is total). This is the parametrization of unitaries by which the enumeration of `lem:value-lower-approx` reaches exact unitaries with Gaussian-rational entries: the Cayley transform of a skew-Hermitian matrix with Gaussian-rational entries has Gaussian-rational entries and the transform is $2$-Lipschitz (bundles `MIPRE_Foundations_ValueApprox_Gaussian` and `MIPRE_Foundations_ValueApprox_Norms`), so rounding $S$ entrywise approximates the unitary (blueprint `lem:rational-pvm-dense`).

The embedded lemmas: `IsSkewHermitian.neg`; `IsSkewHermitian.re_dotProduct_mulVec`, the quadratic form $\langle v, Sv\rangle$ of a skew-Hermitian matrix has real part $0$; `IsSkewHermitian.mulVec_one_add_eq_zero`, $(1+S)v = 0$ forces $v = 0$, whence `isUnit_one_add` and `isUnit_one_sub`, $1 + S$ and $1 - S$ are units; `cayley_eq`, $\mathrm{cayley}(S) = 2(1+S)^{-1} - 1$ when $1 + S$ is a unit; `cayley_mem_unitaryGroup`, the Cayley transform of a skew-Hermitian matrix is unitary; `exists_isSkewHermitian_cayley_eq`, every unitary $U$ with $1 + U$ a unit is $\mathrm{cayley}(S)$ for some skew-Hermitian $S$; `smul_mem_unitaryGroup` and `smul_mul_mul_conjTranspose_smul`, for $\|z\| = 1$ the matrix $zU$ is unitary when $U$ is, and $(zU)\,P\,(zU)^{\mathsf H} = U P U^{\mathsf H}$; `infinite_setOf_norm_eq_one`, the unit circle $\{z : \|z\| = 1\}$ is infinite; and `exists_norm_eq_one_isUnit_one_add_smul`, for every matrix $U$ some unit scalar $z$ makes $1 + zU$ a unit. Together: up to a phase, every unitary is a Cayley transform.

**Formalization Note**. `IsSkewHermitian` is a plain `Prop`-valued definition and unitarity is membership in `Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ`; `cayley` is `noncomputable` because of the matrix inverse, and its unitarity and surjectivity statements are the only places where invertibility of $1 + S$ is used, through `IsUnit`. `IsSkewHermitian.neg` needs no finiteness, `re_dotProduct_mulVec` needs `Fintype n`, and the remaining lemmas also `DecidableEq n`.

definition_title: Projective measurements on $\mathbb{C}^n$ are coordinate patterns in a unitary frame
natural_language_statement:
Let $n$ be a finite index type with decidable equality and $A$ a finite outcome type. `MIPRE.ValueApprox.IsPVM M`, for a family `M : A → Matrix n n ℂ`, is a `Prop`-valued structure with three fields: `conjTranspose_eq`, $(M_a)^{\mathsf H} = M_a$; `mul_self`, $M_a M_a = M_a$; and `sum_eq_one`, $\sum_a M_a = 1$ — the measurement operators of one question of a projective measurement on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$. `MIPRE.ValueApprox.patternProj r a`, for an outcome pattern $r : n \to A$ (with $A$ having decidable equality), is the diagonal matrix projecting onto the coordinates $i$ with $r(i) = a$:
$$\mathrm{patternProj}(r)_a = \mathrm{diag}\bigl(i \mapsto [\,r(i) = a\,]\bigr).$$

The embedded lemmas: `dotProduct_conjTranspose_mul_self`, $\langle v, N^{\mathsf H}N v\rangle = \langle Nv, Nv\rangle$; `ProjectiveMeasurement.isPVM`, the operators of a `MIPRE.ProjectiveMeasurement` on a matrix algebra at any question form an `IsPVM`; `IsPVM.conj`, conjugation $M_a \mapsto U M_a U^{*}$ by a unitary $U$ preserves `IsPVM`; `IsPVM.mul_eq_zero`, distinct outcomes are orthogonal, $M_b M_a = 0$ for $a \ne b$; `isPVM_patternProj`, every pattern family is an `IsPVM`; and the structure theorem `IsPVM.exists_unitary_pattern`: for every `IsPVM M` there are a unitary $U$ (an element of `Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ`) and a pattern $r : n \to A$ with $M_a = U\,\mathrm{patternProj}(r)_a\,U^{*}$ for every $a$. So a projective measurement is exactly "a unitary and a pattern", and enumerating unitaries with Gaussian-rational entries together with patterns enumerates exact projective measurements, the route to approximating the quantum value from below without approximate POVMs, matrix square roots or Naimark dilation (blueprint `lem:rational-pvm-dense`).

**Formalization Note**. `IsPVM` is stated for an arbitrary indexed family rather than for the bundled `MIPRE.ProjectiveMeasurement`, so that it can be asserted of the raw data of an enumerated candidate (`ExactStrategy.IsValid` in the strategy bundle); the unitary of the structure theorem is an element of the subtype `Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ` coerced to a matrix, and `star U` is its conjugate transpose. `patternProj` and the lemmas from `IsPVM.conj` on assume `DecidableEq A`; `IsPVM` itself and `ProjectiveMeasurement.isPVM` do not.

definition_title: Gaussian rationals, and matrices with entries in a subfield of $\mathbb{C}$
natural_language_statement:
The enumeration of `lem:value-lower-approx` ranges over strategies whose matrices and state have entries in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$. `MIPRE.ValueApprox.GaussianRat` is the subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ (a `Subfield ℂ`) whose carrier is the set of $z$ with rational real and imaginary parts, $\exists\, a : \mathbb{Q},\ a = \mathrm{Re}\,z$ and $\exists\, b : \mathbb{Q},\ b = \mathrm{Im}\,z$, together with the closure proofs of a subfield. For a subfield $K$ of $\mathbb{C}$ and a matrix `M : Matrix m n ℂ` over arbitrary index types, `MIPRE.ValueApprox.EntriesIn K M` says that all entries lie in $K$:
$$\mathrm{EntriesIn}(K, M) \iff \forall\, i\, j,\ M_{ij} \in K.$$

The embedded lemmas: for `GaussianRat`, `ratCast_mem`, `I_mem`, `star_mem` (closure under complex conjugation), `mem_iff_exists_eq` ($z \in \mathbb{Q}(i) \iff z = a + b\,i$ for some $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}$) and the density statement `exists_norm_sub_le`: for every $z \in \mathbb{C}$ and $\eta > 0$ there is $w \in \mathbb{Q}(i)$ with $\|z - w\| \le \eta$. For `EntriesIn K`: closure under `add`, `sub`, `smul` by a scalar in $K$, `conjTranspose` (under the hypothesis that $K$ is closed under `star`), `mul`, the identity matrix `one`, the pattern projections `patternProj`, and for square matrices `det_mem`, `adjugate`, `inv` and hence `cayley`: the Cayley transform of a matrix with entries in $K$ has entries in $K$. Finally the rounding lemmas: `exists_entriesIn_norm_sub_le`, every complex matrix is within $\eta$ entrywise of a matrix with Gaussian-rational entries; `exists_forall_mem_norm_sub_le`, the same for vectors; and `IsSkewHermitian.exists_entriesIn_norm_sub_le`, every skew-Hermitian matrix is within $\eta$ entrywise of a skew-Hermitian matrix with Gaussian-rational entries.

**Formalization Note**. `GaussianRat` is a `Subfield ℂ`, so membership is `z ∈ GaussianRat` and the `Subfield` lemmas (`add_mem`, `mul_mem`, `inv_mem`, `sum_mem`) apply; `EntriesIn` takes the subfield as an explicit argument and is a plain universal statement with no finiteness assumption, except that the square-matrix lemmas assume `Fintype n` and `DecidableEq n`. `inv` is Mathlib's matrix inverse, $0$ on a singular matrix, so `EntriesIn.inv` has no invertibility hypothesis, and all rounding bounds are entrywise and non-strict, with $\eta > 0$ strict.

definition_title: Operator-norm estimates for the enumeration of strategies
natural_language_statement:
This bundle contributes no definitions; it is the analytic input of `lem:value-lower-approx`, 24 lemmas in the $L^{2}$ operator norm on complex $n \times n$ matrices (Mathlib's scoped `Matrix.Norms.L2Operator` instance), vectors $x : n \to \mathbb{C}$ being measured in Euclidean space as `toLp 2 x`, written $\|x\|$ below; $n$ and $m$ are finite index types with decidable equality (blueprint `lem:rational-pvm-dense`).

**Vectors and the dot product.** `inner_toLp_toLp` ($\langle x, y\rangle = x^{*}\cdot y$), `norm_sq_toLp` ($\|x\|^{2} = \mathrm{Re}(x^{*}\cdot x)$), `dotProduct_star_self_eq_ofReal`, `norm_toLp_eq_one_of_dotProduct` ($x^{*}\cdot x = 1 \Rightarrow \|x\| = 1$), `norm_toLp_mulVec_le` ($\|Ax\| \le \|A\|\,\|x\|$), `norm_dotProduct_mulVec_le` ($|x^{*}\cdot(Ty)| \le \|T\|\,\|x\|\,\|y\|$), `l2_opNorm_le_of_forall` (if $\|Ax\| \le c\,\|x\|$ for all $x$ with $c \ge 0$ then $\|A\| \le c$), `norm_toLp_le_card_mul_of_forall_norm_le` (entries bounded by $\delta \ge 0$ give $\|v\| \le |n|\,\delta$), and `norm_toLp_normalize_sub_le`: for $\|\psi\| = 1$ and $u \ne 0$, $\|u/\|u\| - \psi\| \le 2\,\|u - \psi\|$.

**The Cayley transform.** `IsSkewHermitian.norm_toLp_le_norm_toLp_one_add_mulVec` ($\|x\| \le \|(1+S)x\|$), `IsSkewHermitian.norm_inv_one_add_le` ($\|(1+S)^{-1}\| \le 1$), the resolvent identity `cayley_sub_cayley`, $\mathrm{cayley}(S) - \mathrm{cayley}(T) = 2\,(1+S)^{-1}(T - S)(1+T)^{-1}$, and `norm_cayley_sub_cayley_le`,
$$\|\mathrm{cayley}(S) - \mathrm{cayley}(T)\| \le 2\,\|S - T\| \quad\text{for skew-Hermitian } S, T.$$

**Entrywise bounds, Kronecker products, unitaries, projections.** `l2_opNorm_le_card_mul_of_entry_le` ($|E_{ij}| \le \delta$ for all $i, j$, with $\delta \ge 0$, gives $\|E\| \le |n|\,\delta$: the cost of rounding a matrix entrywise); `kronecker_one_mulVec` and `one_kronecker_mulVec` (how $X \otimes 1$ and $1 \otimes Y$ act on a vector indexed by $m \times n$), `norm_kronecker_one_le`, `norm_one_kronecker_le` and `norm_kronecker_le` ($\|X \otimes Y\| \le \|X\|\,\|Y\|$); `norm_mul_mul_conjTranspose_sub_le` ($\|VPV^{\mathsf H} - WPW^{\mathsf H}\| \le 2\,\|V - W\|$ when $\|V\|, \|W\|, \|P\| \le 1$); `norm_toLp_mulVec_eq_of_mem_unitaryGroup` and `norm_le_one_of_mem_unitaryGroup` (a unitary preserves the norm of vectors and has norm at most $1$); `norm_le_one_of_isProj` (a self-adjoint idempotent has norm at most $1$) and `IsPVM.norm_le_one` (each operator of an `IsPVM` has norm at most $1$).

**Formalization Note**. The matrix norm is the $L^{2}$ operator norm, enabled by `open scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`, and every vector norm is written through `toLp 2` into `EuclideanSpace ℂ n`, which is why the statements carry `toLp` explicitly; `l2_opNorm_le_of_forall` is the bridge from pointwise bounds to the operator norm. All inequalities are non-strict, with the constants $2$ and $|n| = $ `Fintype.card n` exactly as stated; `IsPVM.norm_sum_le_one`, named in the module docstring, is not among the declarations of this bundle.

definition_title: Gaussian-rational unitaries and projective measurements are dense
natural_language_statement:
This bundle contributes no definitions and two theorems, the density half of `lem:value-lower-approx` (blueprint `lem:rational-pvm-dense`), for a finite index type $n$ with decidable equality and complex $n \times n$ matrices in the $L^{2}$ operator norm.

`MIPRE.ValueApprox.exists_unitary_entriesIn_norm_smul_sub_le`: for every unitary $U$ (an element of `Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ`) and every $\eta > 0$ there are a unit scalar $z \in \mathbb{C}$, $\|z\| = 1$, and a unitary $V$ with entries in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$ (`EntriesIn GaussianRat V`) such that
$$\|z\,U - V\| \le \eta .$$
Up to a unit phase, every unitary is within $\eta$ of a Gaussian-rational unitary.

`MIPRE.ValueApprox.IsPVM.exists_entriesIn_norm_sub_le`: for every family `M : A → Matrix n n ℂ` with `IsPVM M` ($A$ a finite type with decidable equality) and every $\eta > 0$ there is a family $M'$ with `IsPVM M'`, every $M'_a$ having entries in $\mathbb{Q}(i)$, and $\|M_a - M'_a\| \le \eta$ for every outcome $a$: every projective measurement is within $\eta$, element by element, of a projective measurement with Gaussian-rational entries.

As the module docstring records, the first theorem is the Cayley transform of an entrywise rounding of the skew-Hermitian Cayley preimage of $zU$, and the second conjugates the coordinate pattern of `IsPVM.exists_unitary_pattern` by the approximating unitary; both feed the density of exact strategies in the bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_ValueApprox_Strategy`.

**Formalization Note**. This is the point where the Lean route departs from the paper's: the paper rounds the measurement operators themselves and repairs the result into a POVM (its Claims "Stability" and "Density"), whereas here the rounding happens at the level of the skew-Hermitian generator, so that the rounded object is an exact projective measurement and no repair is needed. The phase $z$ is present because $1 + U$ need not be invertible; a suitable unit scalar always makes $1 + zU$ invertible, and conjugation by $zU$ is conjugation by $U$, which is why the second statement carries no phase. Both bounds are non-strict, in the operator norm `Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`, with $\eta > 0$ strict.

definition_title: Exact strategies with unnormalized states, and the quantum value from below
natural_language_statement:
Let $G$ be a game on finite alphabets $X, Y, A, B$ (`MIPRE.Game X Y A B`). This bundle is the mathematical core of `lem:value-lower-approx`: the quantum value exceeds a threshold iff some exact strategy with Gaussian-rational entries does (blueprint `lem:rational-strategies-suffice`).

**Born values on unbundled data.** `MIPRE.ValueApprox.bornValue G P Q ψ`, for operator families `P : X → A → Matrix dA dA ℂ`, `Q : Y → B → Matrix dB dB ℂ` and a vector `ψ : dA × dB → ℂ`, not necessarily normalized, is $\sum_{x,y,a,b}\mu(x,y)\,[D(x,y,a,b)]\,\mathrm{Re}\langle\psi,(P^a_x\otimes Q^b_y)\psi\rangle$; `TensorProductStrategy.value_eq_bornValue` says `S.value` is the `bornValue` of its data.

**Exact strategies.** `MIPRE.ValueApprox.ExactStrategy X Y A B` is a structure of raw data: dimensions `dA`, `dB`, operators `PA : X → A → Matrix (Fin dA) (Fin dA) ℂ` and `PB : Y → B → Matrix (Fin dB) (Fin dB) ℂ`, and an unnormalized state `u : Fin dA × Fin dB → ℂ`. Whether the data is a strategy is the separate `Prop`-structure `ExactStrategy.IsValid c`, with fields `isPVM_A` (every `c.PA x` is an `IsPVM`), `isPVM_B` and `u_ne_zero`; `ExactStrategy.EntriesIn c K` says all entries of `PA`, `PB` and `u` lie in the subfield $K$. The value of the data in $G$ is
$$c.\mathrm{value}(G) = \frac{\mathrm{bornValue}(G,\ c.\mathrm{PA},\ c.\mathrm{PB},\ c.u)}{\mathrm{Re}(u^{*}\cdot u)},$$
a rational function of the entries; `ExactStrategy.ψ c` is the normalized state $\|u\|^{-1}u$ (norm through `toLp 2`), and `ExactStrategy.toStrategy c G hc`, for valid data, is the tensor-product strategy with state $\psi$ and the measurements certified by `hc`. `MIPRE.ValueApprox.pointMeasurement X a₀` is the projective measurement on $\mathbb{C}^{1}$ that always answers $a_0$.

The embedded lemmas are the Lipschitz estimates `abs_re_dotProduct_kronecker_sub_le`, `abs_sum_sub_sum_le` and `abs_bornValue_sub_le` (if every operator moves by at most $\eta$ in operator norm, the operators of the new data are `IsPVM`, and the unit states differ by at most $\eta$, the value moves by at most $|A|\,|B|\cdot 4\eta$); `ψ_unit`, `norm_toLp_ψ`, `value_toStrategy` and `value_eq_bornValue_ψ` (the value of valid data is the value of its strategy); soundness `value_le_quantumValue`, $c.\mathrm{value}(G) \le \mathrm{val}^{*}(G)$ for valid $c$; density `exists_exactStrategy_value_gt`, for every tensor-product strategy $S$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ a valid Gaussian-rational $c$ with $S.\mathrm{value} - \varepsilon < c.\mathrm{value}(G)$; `nonempty_tensorProductStrategy` (a strategy exists when $A$ and $B$ are nonempty); and `lt_quantumValue_iff`: for $A$, $B$ nonempty and every real $t$, $t < \mathrm{val}^{*}(G)$ iff there is a valid $c$ with Gaussian-rational entries and $t < c.\mathrm{value}(G)$.

**Formalization Note**. Validity is kept separate from the data so that the data can be enumerated and validity checked; `value` divides by `(star u ⬝ᵥ u).re`, a total operation in Lean, and is only meaningful under `IsValid`. The biconditional is sharp, with strict inequalities on both sides, because every candidate is exact; this departs from the paper's proof of statement (S) of `cor:mip-re`, which enumerates approximate candidates satisfying relaxed POVM constraints and repairs each by $T \mapsto T^{-1/2}$ conjugation with an explicit slack, so no slack and no positive-semidefiniteness test appear. The Lipschitz constant $4|A||B|$ is crude but sufficient.

definition_title: Transport of games and strategies: relabeling, zero extension and merging of answers
natural_language_statement:
Bookkeeping constructions on strategies under changes of presentation of a game, used to identify a verifier's game with its tabulation as a game description and to compare the same game under different answer-length bounds (blueprint `rem:compression-abstract`). The alphabets $X, Y, A, B$ are finite types.

**On projective measurements** (over any star ring $\mathcal A$, finite outcomes). `ProjectiveMeasurement.reindex P eX eA` relabels questions along any map $e_X : X' \to X$ and answers along an equivalence $e_A : A' \simeq A$, with operators $M_{e_X x'}^{\,e_A a'}$. `ProjectiveMeasurement.extend P ι`, for an embedding $\iota : A \hookrightarrow A'$, puts the zero operator on the new answers: the operator at $\iota a$ is $M^a_x$, and it is $0$ off the range. `ProjectiveMeasurement.merge P r`, for matrices over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ and a map $r : A' \to A$, sums the outcomes with the same image:
$$(\mathrm{merge}\ P\ r)^{\,a}_{x} = \sum_{a' :\ r(a') = a} P^{a'}_{x} .$$

**On tensor-product strategies** for `G : Game X Y A B`: `TensorProductStrategy.copy S G'` (the same data as a strategy for another game on the same alphabets), `relabel S G' eX eY eA eB` (questions along maps, answers along equivalences), `extendAnswers S G' ιA ιB` (zero extension along embeddings) and `mergeAnswers S' G rA rB` (merging along maps to smaller alphabets); each keeps the dimensions and the state.

**On synchronous strategies** for `G : SynchronousGame X A`: `SyncStrategy.copy S G'`, `SyncStrategy.extend S G' ι`, `SyncStrategy.relabel S G' eX eA` (questions along a map, answers along an equivalence), and `SyncStrategy.const G a₀`, the one-dimensional strategy that always answers $a_0$.

The embedded lemmas are the `simp` rules for the operators of `reindex`, `extend` (on and off the range), `merge` and `relabel`; the orthogonality `ProjectiveMeasurement.mul_eq_zero_of_ne`, $M^a_x M^b_x = 0$ for $a \ne b$ on a matrix algebra, which `merge` needs; `value_extendAnswers` and `SyncStrategy.value_extend` (zero extension preserves the value when $G'$ has the same distribution and agrees with $G$ on embedded answers); `value_le_mergeAnswers` (merging can only raise the value when every accepted tuple of the large game is accepted after merging); `SyncStrategy.isPCC_extend` (zero extension preserves the PCC property); and `quantumValue_extendAnswers`: enlarging the answer alphabets by answers that are always rejected leaves $\mathrm{val}^{*}$ unchanged.

**Formalization Note**. Question relabelings are arbitrary maps while answer relabelings are equivalences, which is what the normalization $\sum_a M^a_x = 1$ needs; `extend` is `noncomputable` (it uses `Function.extend`), and `merge` is stated only over matrix algebras because it needs the orthogonality of distinct outcomes. The hypotheses of the value lemmas are pointwise: $\mu' = \mu$ on all question pairs, $D'(x,y,\iota_A a,\iota_B b) = D(x,y,a,b)$, and for `quantumValue_extendAnswers` additionally that $G'$ accepts only pairs in the ranges of the embeddings, with $A$, $B$ nonempty and with decidable equality. `quantumValue_eq_of_equiv`, `quantumValue_mono`, `syncValue_eq_of_equiv` and the lemmas on `relabel` and `const` named in the module docstring are not among the declarations of this bundle.

definition_title: Game descriptions read as synchronous games and games of the foundations
natural_language_statement:
`HaltingGameValue.GameData` (blueprint `def:game-description`, bundle `MIPRE_HaltingGameValue`) is the codable first-order description of a synchronous game: a question alphabet $\{0,\dots,n_X\}$, an answer alphabet $\{0,\dots,n_A\}$, natural-number question weights with their total, and an acceptance set; `GameData.toGame` interprets it in the self-contained vocabulary of `MIPRE.HaltingGameValue`. This bundle reads a description in the vocabulary of the foundations (`MIPRE.SynchronousGame`, `MIPRE.Game`), where the quantum value `MIPRE.quantumValue` lives.

**The two readings.** `HaltingGameValue.GameData.syncGame g` is the `MIPRE.SynchronousGame (Fin (g.nX + 1)) (Fin (g.nA + 1))` with the distribution, decision predicate and synchronicity proof of `g.toGame`, and `HaltingGameValue.GameData.game g` is `g.syncGame.toGame`, a `MIPRE.Game` on the same alphabets. Concretely, with $W$ the total weight,
$$\mu(x,y) = \begin{cases}[\,x = 0 \wedge y = 0\,] & \text{if } W = 0,\\ \mathrm{questionWeight}(x,y)/W & \text{otherwise,}\end{cases}\qquad D(x,y,a,b) = \begin{cases}\mathrm{false} & \text{if } x = y \wedge a \ne b,\\ [\,(x,y,a,b) \in \mathrm{acc}\,] & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$

**The two strategy structures.** `HaltingGameValue.GameData.toSyncStrategy g S` reads a `HaltingGameValue.SyncStrategy g.toGame` (a positive dimension, a question-indexed family of POVMs and a projectivity certificate) as a `MIPRE.SyncStrategy g.syncGame` with the same dimension and the POVM elements as the operators of the projective measurement (self-adjointness and normalization are the POVM's own, projectivity its certificate); `HaltingGameValue.GameData.ofSyncStrategy g S` goes back, with the operators of the projective measurement as POVM elements (positivity from projectivity, via `MIPRE.SyncStrategy.povm`).

The embedded lemmas `game_μ`, `game_D`, `syncGame_μ` and `syncGame_D` are the unfolding equations of the two readings, all by `rfl`.

**Formalization Note**. The two game structures agree field by field, so `syncGame` and `game` are definitions with nothing to prove; the two strategy structures differ in packaging only (POVMs with a projectivity certificate versus a `MIPRE.ProjectiveMeasurement`), and both conversions keep the dimension and the operators, which is what lets `GameData.gameValue_eq_syncValue` (a theorem of the source module, not among the declarations of this bundle) identify the two suprema `HaltingGameValue.gameValue` and `MIPRE.syncValue`. The definitions are marked `noncomputable` (the distribution is real-valued).

definition_title: Raw candidate strategies over the Gaussian integers, and the exact certificate check
natural_language_statement:
The enumeration behind `lem:value-lower-approx` ranges over raw candidates: Gaussian-integer numerators (`GInt`, bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_ValueApprox_RawInt`) over a common denominator $k$, checked in exact integer arithmetic against a game description `g : GameData`.

**List matrices.** `GMat` is `List (List GInt)`, a matrix as a list of rows; `entry M i j` is the $(i,j)$ entry and `vget v i` the $i$-th entry of a list vector, both $0$ when missing; `gsum n f` and `psum n f` are $\sum_{l < n} f(l)$ in `GInt` and in `PInt`.

**Raw candidates.** `RawStrategy` is a structure with fields `k dA dB : ℕ`, `QA QB : List (List GMat)` (numerators of the two players' operators, indexed by question then answer) and `v : List GInt` (numerators of the state, in row-major order $(i,j) \mapsto i\,d_B + j$); `RawStrategy.equivTuple` identifies it with a $6$-tuple and `instPrimcodable` is the induced `Primcodable` instance; `matA r x a`, `matB r y b` read the numerator matrices (empty when missing); and `RawStrategy.interp nX nA r` is the `ExactStrategy` on the alphabets `Fin (nX + 1)`, `Fin (nA + 1)` with every numerator divided by $k$, as complex numbers.

**The check.** `IsHermRaw M d`: $M_{ij} = \overline{M_{ji}}$ for $i, j < d$ (semantic equality `GInt.Eq'`); `IsIdemRaw M d k`: $\sum_{l<d} M_{il}M_{lj} = k\,M_{ij}$, i.e. $M/k$ is idempotent; `IsSumRaw Ms nA d k`: $\sum_{a \le n_A}(M_a)_{ij} = k\,[i = j]$; `IsPVMRaw Ms nA d k`: each of $M_0, \dots, M_{n_A}$ is Hermitian and idempotent and they sum to $k \cdot 1$, so $(M_a/k)_a$ is a projective measurement on $\mathbb{C}^{d}$. `quadRaw A B dA dB v` is the Born numerator $\langle v, (A \otimes B)v\rangle$ in `GInt` and `normRaw v dA dB` the real part of $\langle v, v\rangle$ in `PInt`; `wt g x y` is the question weight of the description (the point mass at $(0,0)$ when the total weight vanishes, as in `GameData.toGame`), `W g` the total weight ($1$ when it vanishes), `Draw g x y a b` the decision predicate on naturals (`false` for $x = y$, $a \ne b$, otherwise membership in the acceptance set), and `numer g r` $= \sum_{x,y}\mathrm{wt}(x,y)\sum_{a,b}[D(x,y,a,b)]\,\mathrm{Re}\langle v,(A^a_x\otimes B^b_y)v\rangle$. `ValueTest g p q r` is $p/q < \mathrm{value}$ cleared of denominators:
$$\bigl(q = 0 \wedge 0 < \mathrm{numer}\bigr)\ \vee\ \bigl(q \ne 0 \wedge p\,W\,k^{2}\,\langle v,v\rangle < q\cdot \mathrm{numer}\bigr),$$
and `Check g p q r` is the conjunction: $0 < k$; `IsPVMRaw` for every question $x \le n_X$ of each player, with dimensions $d_A$ and $d_B$; some entry of $v$ at a row-major index below $d_A d_B$ is nonzero; and `ValueTest`. The six predicates carry `Decidable` instances.

The embedded lemmas are `toC_gsum` and `toInt_psum` (the list sums denote the finite sums) and the `Primrec` proofs of `equivTuple` and of the six projections `k`, `dA`, `dB`, `QA`, `QB`, `v`.

**Formalization Note**. For $q = 0$ the real $p/q$ is $0$ in Lean, which is why the test has a separate clause. Missing list entries read as $0$, so every predicate is total over arbitrary lists; `interp` is `noncomputable` (complex division). The module docstring records that the bundle `RawSemantics` proves `Check g p q r` iff `interp r` is valid with value above $p/q$, and that `RawPrimrec` proves everything here primitive recursive.

definition_title: The certificate check is correct: raw candidates denote valid exact strategies with the claimed value
natural_language_statement:
Two definitions and the correctness theorem of the exact check `Check g p q r` of raw candidates (bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_ValueApprox_RawStrategy`) against the semantics of exact strategies (bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_ValueApprox_Strategy`), for a game description `g : GameData` and naturals $p, q$.

**Denotations.** `MIPRE.ValueApprox.mat M d k` is the complex $d \times d$ matrix (`Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℂ`) with entries $M_{ij}/k$, for a list matrix $M$ and a denominator $k$; `MIPRE.ValueApprox.vec dA dB v k` is the state on `Fin dA × Fin dB` with $(i,j) \mapsto v(i\,d_B + j)/k$.

The embedded lemmas read each clause of `Check` as the corresponding statement about the denotation, under $k \ne 0$: `isHermRaw_iff` ($(\mathrm{mat}\,M)^{\mathsf H} = \mathrm{mat}\,M$), `isIdemRaw_iff` ($\mathrm{mat}\,M \cdot \mathrm{mat}\,M = \mathrm{mat}\,M$), `isSumRaw_iff` ($\sum_a \mathrm{mat}\,M_a = 1$), `isPVMRaw_iff` (the family of `mat`s is an `IsPVM`), `vec_ne_zero_iff` (the state is nonzero iff some numerator at a row-major index below $d_A d_B$ is), `dotProduct_vec_self` and `re_dotProduct_vec_self` ($\mathrm{Re}\langle v, v\rangle = \mathrm{normRaw}/k^{2}$), `dotProduct_kronecker_vec` and `re_dotProduct_kronecker_vec` ($\mathrm{Re}\langle v,(\mathrm{mat}\,A \otimes \mathrm{mat}\,B)v\rangle = \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{quadRaw}/k^{4}$), `normRaw_pos`; `GameData.one_le_W`, `GameData.game_μ_eq` ($\mu(x,y) = \mathrm{wt}(x,y)/W$) and `GameData.game_D_eq` ($D = \mathrm{Draw}$); `toInt_numer`, `interp_bornValue` and `interp_value` (the value of `interp r` is $\mathrm{numer}/(W\,k^{2}\,\mathrm{normRaw})$), `valueTest_iff` (for $k \ne 0$ and a nonzero state, `ValueTest` iff $p/q <$ value); and the auxiliary `toC_gsum_fin`, `toInt_psum_fin`, `div_sq_eq_div_iff`, `mat_mul_mat_apply`. The conclusion is `MIPRE.ValueApprox.check_iff_interp`:
$$\mathrm{Check}(g,p,q,r) \iff (r.\mathrm{interp}\ g.n_X\ g.n_A).\mathrm{IsValid}\ \wedge\ \frac{p}{q} < (r.\mathrm{interp}\ g.n_X\ g.n_A).\mathrm{value}(g.\mathrm{game}).$$
Together with the soundness and density of exact strategies, this yields in the next bundle `exists_check_iff`: some raw candidate passes the check iff $p/q < \mathrm{val}^{*}(G_g)$, the semantic content of the semidecision procedure of `lem:value-lower-approx`.

**Formalization Note**. `interp r` unfolds to `mat` and `vec` on the numerator matrices and the state, so every lemma is stated about `mat` and `vec` and transferred; $p/q$ is real division with Lean's convention $p/0 = 0$, matched by the $q = 0$ clause of `ValueTest`; the hypothesis $k \ne 0$ of the clause lemmas is supplied by the clause $0 < k$ of `Check`, so `check_iff_interp` itself has no side condition. `mat` and `vec` are `noncomputable` (complex division).

definition_title: Every Gaussian-rational exact strategy is a raw candidate, and the semidecision criterion for the quantum value
natural_language_statement:
This bundle contributes no definitions and five theorems, closing the semantic analysis of the raw-candidate check for `lem:value-lower-approx`.

`natCast_mul_ratCast_den`: $\mathrm{den}(a)\cdot a = \mathrm{num}(a)$ in $\mathbb{C}$ for a rational $a$. `exists_common_den`: finitely many Gaussian rationals (a `Finset ℂ` whose elements lie in `GaussianRat`) have a common denominator, some natural $k > 0$ such that for each of them $k z$ is the complex number of a Gaussian integer (`GInt.toC w` for some $w$). `getD_ofFn`: `(List.ofFn f).getD i d = f i` for $i$ in range. `exists_rawStrategy_interp_eq`: every exact strategy `c : ExactStrategy (Fin (nX + 1)) (Fin (nX + 1)) (Fin (nA + 1)) (Fin (nA + 1))` with `c.EntriesIn GaussianRat` is `r.interp nX nA` for some raw candidate $r$. Finally `MIPRE.ValueApprox.exists_check_iff`, for a game description `g : GameData` and naturals $p, q$:
$$\bigl(\exists\, r : \mathrm{RawStrategy},\ \mathrm{Check}(g,p,q,r)\bigr) \iff \frac{p}{q} < \mathrm{val}^{*}(g.\mathrm{game}).$$

As the module docstring records, the forward direction is the correctness of the check (`check_iff_interp`) with the soundness of exact strategies, and the converse is the density of Gaussian-rational exact strategies (`lt_quantumValue_iff`) with `exists_rawStrategy_interp_eq`. The left-hand side is a search over a `Primcodable` type for a decidable predicate, so this is the semantic content of the semidecision procedure for $\mathrm{val}^{*}(G) > p/q$.

**Formalization Note**. $p/q$ is real division, $p/0 = 0$ by Lean's convention, so the case $q = 0$ asks whether $\mathrm{val}^{*} > 0$; $\mathrm{val}^{*}$ is `MIPRE.quantumValue` of `g.game`, the reading of the description as a `MIPRE.Game` (bundle `MIPRE_Foundations_GameDescription`); the alphabets `Fin (nX + 1)` and `Fin (nA + 1)` are never empty, which is what `lt_quantumValue_iff` needs. The common denominator is a natural number $k > 0$, so the numerators are Gaussian integers represented in `GInt`, and `exists_rawStrategy_interp_eq` is an equality of `ExactStrategy` structures, dimensions included.
